title: Video Editor | European Creative Team
description:
Nordband is looking for a full time Video Editor to join our European creative pod and help us produce high performing video ads across our existing European markets.



You’ll work closely with a dedicated Creative Strategist, Graphic Designer, and the rest of the creative team. The Creative Strategist will lead the overall direction and testing strategy, while your responsibility will be to turn concepts, briefs, scripts, and raw UGC into strong video ads built to perform.



This is not a role for someone who only waits for footage and instructions. We want someone who can execute what is requested, but also think independently, bring ideas to the table, and continuously improve the creative output.



Responsibilities

- Edit high performing video ads primarily for Meta.

- Turn raw UGC and product footage into conversion focused ads with strong hooks, pacing, storytelling, and CTAs.

- Execute concepts, briefs, revisions, and requests from the Creative Strategist with speed and accuracy.

- Work closely with the Creative Strategist to develop and test new hooks, angles, structures, and concepts.

- Study winning creatives and use those learnings to create new variations and iterations.

- Bring your own creative ideas and suggest improvements when you see opportunities.

- Collaborate with our Graphic Designer and UGC team when additional assets or footage are needed.

- Localize and adapt videos for different European markets.

- Add captions, motion graphics, sound effects, music, AI voiceovers, and other elements when needed.

- Manage multiple projects at the same time while maintaining strong quality and organization.

- Iterate quickly based on feedback and performance data.



Markets & Languages

You’ll be creating and adapting ads for markets including:

- Sweden

- Norway

- Denmark

- Germany

- Netherlands



Creatives may be produced in:

- Swedish

- Norwegian

- Danish

- German

- Dutch

- English



You do not need to speak all of these languages fluently, but you must be comfortable working with translated scripts, subtitles, voiceovers, and multilingual content.



What We’re Looking For

- Proven experience editing performance driven video ads for eCommerce or DTC brands.

- Strong understanding of Meta Ads and direct response creative.

- Experience turning UGC into ads that are designed to convert.

- Strong understanding of hooks, retention, pacing, storytelling, and customer psychology.

- Ability to work fast without sacrificing quality.

- Comfortable following direction and executing exactly what is requested when needed.

- At the same time, able to think independently and contribute your own ideas.

- Comfortable receiving direct feedback and iterating quickly.

- Strong proficiency in Premiere Pro, After Effects, CapCut, or similar tools.

- Reliable, organized, and comfortable working remotely.

- Interested in a full time, long term position.

Nice to Have

- Experience with AI video tools, AI voiceovers, or automated creative workflows.

- Experience working with multiple European markets.

- Background in creative strategy or performance marketing.

- Experience analyzing ad performance and turning insights into new creatives.

- Experience working closely with Creative Strategists.



The Team

You’ll be part of a dedicated European creative pod consisting of a Creative Strategist, Graphic Designer, and Video Editors, with the wider creative department overseen by the company leadership.

You’ll have access to winning ads, performance data, UGC, creative references, and clear strategic direction.



The goal is for the team to work as one unit. The Creative Strategist sets the direction, but everyone is expected to contribute ideas and help improve the overall creative output.



Long Term Opportunity

We’re building this team for the long term.

As Nordband continues to scale across Europe, there will be opportunities to take on more responsibility and grow into more senior creative positions.



We’re not looking for someone who wants to edit videos for a few months and move on. We want someone ambitious who wants to become an important part of the creative team and grow together with the brand.

title: B2B Appointment Setter: Cold and Warm Calls
description:
About Built For B2B

Built For B2B (BFB2B) is a B2B outbound agency with offices in Belfast and New York. We run cold
 and LinkedIn campaigns that book sales meetings for B2B companies, mostly in the US. One campaign built over $1.3M in pipeline in 45 days.



We're adding phone to our outbound, for our own pipeline and for our clients. A fast call to someone who's just replied, or a sharp cold call to a fresh list, books meetings that
 and LinkedIn alone miss. That's where you come in.



The role

You call prospects and book qualified sales meetings. Two kinds of call: warm calls to people who've just replied to our clients'
 or LinkedIn campaigns, and cold calls to fresh lists. You'll dial for BFB2B's own pipeline and for our clients, each with its own offer, script and calendar.



This is a high-volume outbound phone role, calling founders, owners and executives, mostly in the US. Warm leads always come first, because speed decides most of them. Full-time, fully remote, US Eastern hours.



What you'll do

• Call every warm lead within 15 minutes of them landing in your queue, read their reply first, and turn it into a booked meeting.

• Fill the rest of your shift with cold calls: 150+ dials a day through our power dialer.

• Call through the lists we build for each campaign, including accounts already in our
 and LinkedIn sequences.

• Get past gatekeepers and reach the actual decision-maker.

• Open fast, earn the next 30 seconds and qualify against each campaign's criteria (company size, role, need, timing).

• Handle objections live: "not interested", "just send me an
", "we already have someone", "what does it cost?", "call me next quarter".

• Switch cleanly between different clients' offers and scripts in the same week.

• Book meetings straight into the right calendar, then confirm and remind so they show up.

• Leave sharp voi
s and set callbacks you actually keep.

• Chase referrals ("you need to speak to Sarah") and turn them into meetings.

• Log every call, outcome and note in the CRM.

• Post an end-of-day report in Slack: warm leads called, cold dials, conversations, meetings booked, shows, blockers.

• Tell us what's landing and what isn't so we can sharpen scripts and lists.



What you must have

• 2+ years of B2B outbound calling and appointment setting to US, UK or Australian decision-makers.

• Proven cold calling experience. Warm-lead calls are part of the job, but inbound, customer service or collections work alone does not count.

• Clear, confident spoken English that holds a real conversation with a US founder or executive.

• You handle objections and gatekeepers live, without retreating to the script.

• Numbers you can stand behind: dials per day, meetings booked per month and show rate in your last role.

• At least one recording of a real outbound call you made.

• Experience with a power dialer and a CRM (HubSpot, GoHighLevel, Pipedrive or similar).

• A proper home setup: reliable laptop, 25 Mbps+ internet, backup power and backup internet, noise-cancelling USB headset, quiet room.

• Available full-time on US Eastern hours, on the phones for your whole shift. Remote does not mean flexible availability.

Nice to have

• Agency experience, calling for several clients at once.

• Calling leads who replied to cold
 or LinkedIn campaigns.

• Booking meetings with C-suite and senior executives.

• Experience selling into B2B services, SaaS, IT, trades, or government and education.

• Hands-on with Orum, Nooks, Aircall, JustCall, Kixie or a similar dialer.

• Comfortable pulling contact data from Apollo or similar tools.



What you'll use:

Power dialer (we provide)

Calling, recording, voi
 drops

HubSpot

CRM, call logging, meeting records

Smartlead / PlusVibe, HeyReach

Reading a warm lead's
 or LinkedIn reply before you call

Apollo

Contact data and phone numbers

Google Workspace


 and calendars

Slack

Team chat and end-of-day reports

Asana

Tasks and client projects



Hours, pay and how you're measured

• Hours: full-time, 40 hours a week, Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm US Eastern.

• Base pay: $900 to $1,200 USD a month, depending on experience. Paid monthly in USD.

• Bonus: $25 USD for every qualified meeting you book that shows up. Uncapped.

• Start: one paid trial week, then a long-term contractor role.

• Growth: rate review after 90 days of hitting targets.



You'll be judged on these numbers:

Metric

Target

Time to call a warm lead (in shift)

Under 15 minutes

Warm leads turned into booked meetings

50%+

Cold dials per day

150+

Cold decision-maker conversations per day

15+

Cold-call meetings booked per week

Booked meetings that show up

Calls logged in the CRM

Every working day

title: LinkedIn outreach sender for US staffing niche, $240 a month plus $35 per meeting

Stratos B2B delivers qualified trades candidates (electricians, HVAC techs, welders, plumbers) to US staffing agencies. The offer to agencies: 15 qualified candidates in 30 days. If we miss it, we keep working free until we hit it.



Your job: send connection requests and short messages on LinkedIn from your own real profile. I write the copy and build the prospect lists (owners of US staffing agencies). You send the messages, answer replies in your own words, and book short intro meetings. Everything runs from your real profile and your own hands. No automation software, no borrowed accounts, this is the one thing I am strict about.



The money:



1. $240 per month base pay, paid as $60 every week in arrears for completing your daily sending shifts

2. $35 on top for every qualified meeting that actually happens (a no show means a free rebook)

3. Realistic month one at target pace: 8 to 12 held meetings, so $520 to $660 total for part-time hours

4. Payment via international bank transfer or GCash, your choice, every week without chasing



The daily shift, about 1 to 2 hours, 5 days a week:



1. Send around 15 connection requests and messages from my lists

2. Update your tracker as you go

3. Answer replies in your own words, using my templates as the base



What you get from me:



1. A fresh verified prospect list every week. You never chase your own leads

2. All message copy written for you

3. An offer that is easy to stand behind. The guarantee does the selling

4. Fast, reliable weekly pay and a long term arrangement if it works



I am early and will not pretend otherwise. No big case studies yet. What I can promise: real lists, real copy, and fast payment for real results.



You would be a fit if:



1. Your LinkedIn is real, active, and has 500+ connections

2. You write English at native level and can chat with US business owners without sounding like a script

3. You can give this a steady 1 to 2 hours most days



HOW TO APPLY: send an
 to hello at stratosb2b dot net with the subject "LinkedIn sender application" and answer these 4 questions:



1. How many product lines or companies do you represent right now?

2. What share of your week would this be?

3. Drop your LinkedIn profile link.

4. Write a sample connection request for a staffing agency owner in Dallas. Max 300 characters. Start your answer with the word TULIP so I know you read this far.



If your sample sounds like a real person, we talk this week.

title: Financial Controller - US GAAP
description:
Position Overview:

The Controller exists to own the financial backbone of a scaling, multi-company organization — keeping the books accurate, timely, and audit-ready every month. Working remotely from the Philippines on US business hours, the role starts inside MedPro Disposal and extends across Accordant Capital’s portfolio of operating companies, including MP1 Solutions and future portfolio additions. Reporting to the US-based VP of Finance, this is a hands-on role: owning the full accounting cycle and close, developing the controls and processes a growing business needs, and bringing modern ERP/FP&A tooling, AI-enabled automation, and operating discipline (EOS or a similar system) to the accounting function. Success looks like a close that runs like clockwork across every company, consolidations that reconcile cleanly, and a well-run accounting operation the executive team can rely on.



Key Responsibilities:

● Own the full accounting cycle — general ledger, accounts payable/receivable, payroll (US payroll via third-party provider), and month-end close

● Communication: Excellent written and spoken English



● Work setup: Able to work US Central business hours (PH night shift) full-time; dedicated home office with reliable primary and backup internet and power



Big Pluses:

title: Lead Generation Specialist
description:
About Focusly

Focusly helps Shopify brands turn their
 list into a revenue channel. We build and run
 marketing for ecommerce stores, and we design and develop the websites those stores run on.



Our clients range from founders launching their first Shopify store to established brands who want their
 program run properly. Most of them come to us for one of two things:
 marketing that pays for itself, or a store that converts.



_______________



The Role

We are hiring a Lead Generation Specialist to own the top of our sales pipeline. Your job is to find Shopify store owners who need
 marketing, new website, or social media marketing, start conversations with them, and hand qualified leads to our team to close.



This is a hunting role, not a list-building role. You will be measured on qualified conversations booked, not on the size of your spreadsheet. You will work directly with the founder and have a real say in how our outbound engine is built.



_______________



Who you'll be finding?

Our best leads are Shopify merchants, or people about to become one. You will target four profiles:



1.Already doing
 marketing

-Running a Shopify/WooCommerce/Magento store with Klaviyo, Mailchimp or similar; sending campaigns but flows, segmentation or revenue per send are weak



2.New to
 marketing

-Running a Shopify store with a growing customer list but no flows, no regular campaigns, or just installed an
 platform



3.Wants to launch a Shopify store

-Selling on Etsy, Amazon, Instagram or a legacy platform; planning to move to Shopify or launch a new brand



4.Needs a better website

-Existing store with a dated theme, poor mobile experience or low conversion rate



A good lead is a decision-maker (founder, owner, marketing lead) at a store doing enough volume to justify an agency, who has a clear problem we solve. You will help us sharpen this profile as you learn what converts.



_______________



What you'll do?

• Build targeted lists of Shopify merchants who match our lead profiles, using tools such as Apollo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Store Leads, BuiltWith and Shopify app directories (or any tool that you're proficient with)

• Qualify each lead before outreach: confirm they are on Shopify (or moving to it), check their
 setup, estimate store size, and find the decision-maker

• Run multi-channel outbound: cold
 sequences, LinkedIn outreach and, where it fits, Instagram or phone

• Write and test outreach copy and sequences, and keep improving reply and meeting rates

• Book discovery calls for the founder and sales team, and make sure every booked lead is briefed and shows up

• Keep the CRM clean and current: every lead, touchpoint, status and next step logged

• Report weekly on pipeline numbers: leads sourced, contacted, replied, qualified and booked

• Spot patterns in what converts and feed that back into our targeting, messaging and offers

• Keep deliverability healthy: domain warm-up, sending limits, bounce and spam-rate monitoring



_______________



Must have

• 3 to 5 years in lead generation, SDR or outbound sales, with a track record you can show in numbers (leads sourced, reply rates, meetings booked)

• Experience selling to ecommerce or DTC brands, or to agencies that serve them

• Working knowledge of Shopify: you can look at a store and tell whether it is on Shopify, what apps it runs, and roughly how big it is

• Enough understanding of
 marketing to spot a weak program and talk about flows, campaigns and list growth without a script

• Hands-on with at least one prospecting stack: Apollo, Lemlist, Instantly, Smartlead, Clay, LinkedIn Sales Navigator or similar

• Strong written English: your outreach copy is short, specific and gets replies

• Comfortable with a CRM such as HubSpot, Pipedrive or GoHighLevel, and disciplined about keeping it current

• Self-managing: you set weekly targets, hit them, and tell us early when something is not working



_______________



Nice to have

• You have worked at an
 marketing agency or a Shopify agency

• You have used Klaviyo, Mailchimp or Omnisend and know the ecommerce
 landscape

• You have sold website or Shopify development services

• You can run basic phone or video qualification calls

• You have built lists with Store Leads, BuiltWith, Clay or similar enrichment tools



_______________



How to apply?

Send the following to us:

1. Your CV or LinkedIn profile

2. Your numbers from your last lead generation role: leads sourced per month, average reply rate, meetings booked per month, and how you qualified a lead (Portfolio)

3. A short note on how you would find 50 Shopify stores that are new to
 marketing, and which tools you would use

4. One cold
 you would send to a Shopify store owner who has a customer list but no
 flows (under 120 words)

Use the subject line "Lead Generation Specialist - [Your name]". Applications without items 1 to 4 will not be reviewed.

We will reply to shortlisted candidates within 5 business days with a short screening call.

Architectural 3D Renderer & Visualization Specialist



About DivFit



DivFit is a custom fitness space design and installation company specializing in high-end residential and commercial gyms. We work alongside homeowners, architects, interior designers, builders, and developers to create fitness spaces that are as thoughtfully designed as any other room in a home or building.



We believe the gym should never be an afterthought.



From equipment selection and custom finishes to flooring, lighting, wall treatments, and overall aesthetics, we bring every element together to create spaces that are both functional and visually exceptional.



As we continue to grow, we’re looking for a talented Architectural 3D Renderer & Visualization Specialist to help bring our clients’ visions to life.



About the Role



We’re looking for someone with a strong eye for architecture, interior design, and visual storytelling.



You’ll work closely with our design team to transform architectural plans, equipment layouts, and design concepts into realistic 3D renderings that allow clients to experience their fitness spaces before construction begins.



This role goes beyond simply placing gym equipment into a room. We want someone who understands materials, textures, lighting, proportions, and how individual design elements come together to create a cohesive space.



Your work will play a major role in our client presentations, design process, and overall customer experience.



Key Responsibilities



* Create photorealistic 3D renderings of custom residential and commercial fitness spaces.

* Translate architectural floor plans, CAD drawings, and design concepts into accurate 3D environments.

* Model and incorporate fitness equipment from manufacturer specifications, CAD files, and existing 3D assets.

* Develop realistic materials, lighting, flooring, wall treatments, mirrors, and architectural details.

* Collaborate with our internal team, architects, builders, and interior designers to refine designs.

* Produce multiple design concepts, perspectives, and finish options for client presentations.

* Make revisions based on client feedback and project changes.

* Maintain an organized library of equipment models, textures, materials, and rendering assets.

* Help develop compelling visual content for DivFit’s website, social media, and marketing materials.



Qualifications



Required:



* Strong portfolio demonstrating high-quality architectural or interior renderings.

* Proficiency in one or more 3D modeling and rendering platforms such as SketchUp, 3ds Max, Blender, Revit, Lumion, Enscape, V-Ray, or Twinmotion.

* Understanding of architectural drawings, spatial relationships, materials, and realistic lighting.

* Strong attention to detail and ability to create visually accurate environments.

* Ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines.

* Willingness to collaborate, accept feedback, and continuously improve designs.



Preferred:



* Experience in residential architecture, interior design, or commercial visualization.

* Familiarity with AutoCAD, Revit, or other architectural design software.

* Experience importing, modifying, and creating custom 3D equipment models.

* Knowledge of modern interior design, architectural finishes, and lighting design.

* Experience producing walkthrough animations or virtual tours.

* Interest in fitness, architecture, and high-end design.



A degree in architecture or design is welcome but not required. We’re far more interested in your portfolio, creativity, technical ability, and attention to detail.



What We’re Looking For



We’re not looking for someone who simply knows how to use rendering software.



We’re looking for someone who can look at an empty room, understand the design intent, and help turn it into something exceptional.



Someone who notices when a light fixture is out of place, when a material doesn’t work with the overall aesthetic, or when a different camera angle could completely change how a space is presented.



We value creativity, initiative, attention to detail, and people who take pride in their work.



Why DivFit?



DivFit is a growing company working on unique fitness spaces throughout the Mountain West.



You’ll have the opportunity to work on projects ranging from custom home gyms to large commercial fitness facilities, collaborate with talented designers and builders, and have a direct impact on the spaces we create.



We’re building a company that approaches fitness spaces differently, and we’re looking for someone who wants to be part of that.



How to Apply



Please submit your resume and a portfolio showcasing your best architectural or interior visualization work.



We’re especially interested in seeing photorealistic interior renderings, examples of lighting and material work, and projects demonstrating your attention to architectural detail.



Portfolio quality matters more to us than years of experience.

 experience

title: Property Maintenance & Field Operations Supervisor / Manager
description:
Barrister Premier Properties, LLC

Mandeville / Covington — Northshore Louisiana



Barrister Premier Properties, LLC is seeking an experienced, hands-on Property Maintenance & Field Operations Supervisor / Manager to take ownership of maintenance and field operations across our portfolio of multifamily apartments, hotels, shopping centers, commercial properties, and tenant spaces throughout the Northshore.



We are looking for someone with strong construction and property maintenance experience who can diagnose problems, determine the correct repair solution, lead a 3–4 person in-house maintenance crew, manage work orders, procure materials, and personally perform or assist with repairs when needed.



Key Responsibilities



-Manage, assign, prioritize, and track daily maintenance work orders.

-Lead, supervise, and hold accountable a 3–4 person in-house maintenance crew.

-Diagnose building, construction, and maintenance issues and determine the appropriate repair solution.

-Create scopes of work, material lists, and basic material takeoffs.

-Purchase and stage materials ahead of scheduled work and respond quickly to emergency material needs.

-Perform hands-on repairs and maintenance alongside the crew when necessary.

-Conduct regular property walks and inspections to identify maintenance needs before they become larger problems.

-Perform tenant and resident move-out inspections and coordinate turnover work.

-Establish and maintain preventative maintenance schedules across the portfolio.

-Respond to emergency maintenance issues and prioritize work based on urgency, safety, property damage exposure, and operational impact.

-Track outstanding repairs and ensure work is completed properly, timely, and to company standards.

-Coordinate with outside subcontractors when work requires specialized trades or additional manpower.

-Verify completed work and maintain accountability for quality, materials, labor, and company resources.

-Take full ownership of maintenance issues from initial diagnosis through final completion.



Qualifications



-5+ years of experience in construction, property maintenance, facilities maintenance, or maintenance supervision.

-Strong working knowledge of multiple trades, including:

            -Carpentry and general construction

            -Plumbing

            -Electrical

            -HVAC

            -Drywall

            -Painting and finishes

-Proven ability to lead and manage maintenance or construction personnel.

-Experience preparing scopes of work, material takeoffs, and purchasing materials.

-Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving ability.

-Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple active work orders and properties simultaneously.

-Comfortable working in the field daily and performing hands-on work when required.

-Reliable transportation and a clean driving record.

-Strong communication skills and professional presence when interacting with tenants, residents, vendors, subcontractors, and company personnel.



Ideal Candidate



-We are looking for someone who is hands-on, dependable, organized, decisive, and accountable.

-The right candidate should be able to walk into a property, identify the problem, determine the appropriate solution, obtain the necessary materials, assign or perform the work, and make sure the job is completed correctly.

-You should be comfortable making decisions in the field, working under pressure, managing competing priorities, leading a crew, and treating company properties, materials, equipment, and resources as if they were your own.

-We want someone who does not simply identify problems or pass them along. We are looking for someone who takes ownership of the problem and drives it through completion.

-This position is critical to establishing and maintaining a reliable, organized, responsive, and accountable in-house property maintenance operation across the Barrister Premier Properties portfolio.

### 3. Customer Screening, Contracts & Payments

- Track contract completion and customer compliance.

- Coordinate rental invoices and payment reminders.

- Monitor overdue payments and follow up with customers professionally.

- Maintain accurate and confidential customer records.



### 4.
, Phone & Customer Support

s, phone calls, and customer messages.

- Respond promptly and professionally to customer inquiries.

- Resolve common customer concerns and escalate serious issues to management.

- Maintain excellent customer relationships throughout the rental period.

### 5. Social Media & Marketing Support

 Marketplace rental listings.

 and Instagram.

- Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

 Marketplace

- Is hungry to learn, grow, and improve.

- Understands that customer service and sales are equally important.

title: Transaction Coordinator
description:
Position Overview

We are seeking a detail-oriented, highly organized Transaction Coordinator to manage our real estate transactions from contract to close. You will play a pivotal role in ensuring smooth operations, maintaining accurate compliance files in SkySlope, tracking critical dates, and keeping all parties informed throughout the escrow process.



Experience with eXp Realty workflows and compliance standards is a strong preference.



Key Responsibilities

Daily & Ongoing Coordination

 & Communication: Serve as a primary contact for transaction-related
s. Clear document requirements, proactively follow up on missing files, and chase down outstanding signatures.



SkySlope Management: Upload, organize, and assign documents to the correct files daily. Continuously update transaction statuses to ensure compliance.



Document & Signature Coordination: Prepare and send document packages for signatures (e.g., SPDS, CLUE, BINSR, disclosures). Ensure all executed forms are promptly uploaded to SkySlope.



Transaction Tracking: Maintain the central tracking spreadsheet daily with current file statuses, received/missing documents, and signature status.



Note: Record septic inspection reports on the exact date received.



File Audits & Compliance: Routinely review active listing and under-contract files to identify missing or incomplete items, issuing outstanding requirement lists as needed.



Special Projects: Complete specialized file reviews and disclosures, including Onsite/Septic, Solar transfer, and Well documentation for under-contract properties.



Weekly & Closing Reviews

Upcoming Closing Review (Every Monday): Conduct a thorough audit of all files scheduled to close the following week. Ensure all required compliance documents and forms are complete (excluding FWT, Final HUD, and checks). Promptly follow up on missing items.



Closing Updates (Weekly / Upon Closing): Closely monitor files scheduled to close in the current week. Once officially closed, update the tracking spreadsheet with the closing date and flag any lingering post-closing requirements.



Qualifications & Requirements

Experience: 1–3+ years of experience as a Real Estate Transaction Coordinator or Compliance Specialist.



eXp Realty Familiarity: Prior experience navigating eXp Realty's compliance systems, file structures, and state-specific forms is highly preferred (nice to have).



Platform Proficiency: Advanced hands-on experience with SkySlope, standard e-signature tools, and spreadsheet management (Google Sheets / Excel).



Document Knowledge: Strong understanding of standard real estate contracts and disclosure forms (e.g., SPDS, CLUE, BINSR, Well/Septic, Solar).



Skills: Exceptional organizational skills, high attention to detail, proactive follow-through, and strong written communication skills.





Please include "Leverage Agent - Transaction Coordinator" at the subject line.

title: Customer Service Representative — E-commerce, Email Support
description:
We are a US based ecom store doing 30 to 40 orders a day. We already have

one customer service rep and we are looking for a second, so that our

customers always get an answer, every day, without gaps.



Being in the Philippines works well for this role.



WHAT YOU WILL DO



- Answer customer
s. Where is my order, can I change my address,

  I want to return this, the size does not fit.

- Check tracking before you answer. Every single time. Most of our

  questions are answered by looking at where the parcel actually is.

- Log every conversation in our customer service sheet: the customer,

  the order number, the reason, what they asked, what you replied,

  and whether it is closed.

- Process refunds when our rules say so, and log the product, the

  amount and the real reason behind it. This feeds our quality

  reporting, so it has to be accurate.

- Follow up. Any ticket that is not closed within 3 days gets chased.

  The sheet turns red when you forget, so there is nowhere to hide.

- Take requests from our supply chain manager in Slack and
 the

  customer on his behalf, using the information he gives you.

- Work alternating days with our other rep so our inbox is never

  left sitting over a weekend.



HOW WE MEASURE YOU



1. Every customer
 answered within 24 hours: 100 percent

2. Tickets still open after 3 days: 0

3. Every refund logged with the product and the real reason: 100 percent

4. Issues escalated to the owner that you could have solved yourself:

   as close to 0 as possible



WHAT YOU NEED



- Experience in e-commerce customer service. You have handled an inbox

  before and you know what an angry customer sounds like.

- Excellent written English. Our customers are American women and most

  of them are over 40. They notice tone. They are patient if you are

  honest with them and they are not if you sound like a robot.

- You read tracking information before you answer, not after.

- Comfortable in Google Sheets. Everything is already built for you.

- Available 6 days a week, alternating with our other rep.



WHAT WE DO NOT WANT



Someone who refunds a customer just to end the conversation. Refunding

is easy. Keeping a customer who was about to be disappointed is the

job.



HOW TO APPLY



Watch this short video before you apply. It is under 3 minutes.

I explain the role myself, and at the end I tell you exactly what

I need you to include in your message.







I only read applications from people who watched it.

About the role



We're a US direct-to-consumer supplement brand selling on Shopify, largely on subscription.



You will own the customer support inbox. This is not a "reply to whatever comes in" role — you'll work from documented templates, a defined brand voice, and firm rules about what we can and cannot say about the product. Most of the volume is repetitive (order status, shipping, cancellations, refunds), so the job is about accuracy, speed, and judgment on the 10% that isn't routine.



What you'll do

Work the shared Gmail inbox every weekday

Answer order status, shipping delays, tracking, lost packages, and returns

Manage subscriptions: skips, date changes, swaps, and cancellations. Save the ones you can using our retention offers; process the rest quickly and without friction

Look up orders and issue refunds or replacements in Shopify

Handle money-back-guarantee requests according to policy

Use AI-assisted drafting (we'll train you on our setup) — then verify every fact before sending. Draft speed matters; sending a wrong order number matters more

Never make health claims. We do not tell customers the product treats, cures, or prevents any condition, and we never give medical or dosing advice. Anything in that territory gets a scripted response and an escalation. This is a legal line, not a style preference — it's the one rule that gets someone removed from the inbox

Keep the inbox tagged and clean; zero emails older than [24] hours

Flag recurring complaints weekly so we can fix the root cause

title: Accounting Manager
description:
Position Overview:

We're looking for a strong, self-directed Accounting Manager to own the full financial operations of two service companies under one parent LLC. This is not a data-entry role. You will be responsible for keeping the books accurate every day, making sure payroll and payroll taxes are handled correctly, tracking our debt obligations, and giving the Owner a clear picture of profitability and cash flow. The right person spots problems before they become problems and works without being told what to do next. This role reports directly to the Owner.



Key Responsibilities:



Daily Bookkeeping & Reconciliation



Reconcile all bank and credit card accounts daily using QuickBooks bank feeds, and categorize transactions accurately.

Investigate and resolve discrepancies the same day they appear.

Maintain clean, separate books for two entities.



Payroll & Payroll Taxes



Process weekly/bi-weekly payroll accurately and on schedule.

Calculate, file, and pay US payroll taxes on time, including federal withholding, FICA, FUTA (Form 940), quarterly Form 941, NC state withholding, and NC unemployment.

Maintain payroll tax deposit schedules and make sure there are zero late filings or penalties.



Job Profitability



Track and report profitability by job, service type, and client for both residential and commercial services.

Analyze labor, supply, and overhead costs against job revenue, and flag underperforming jobs or pricing issues to the Owner.



Cash Flow Forecasting



Build and maintain a rolling 13-week cash flow forecast.

Project upcoming obligations (payroll, taxes, loan remittances, vendor bills) and alert the Owner to potential shortfalls in advance.



Debt & Financing Management



Properly record and track merchant cash advances (MCAs) and Stripe Capital loans, including the original balance, fees/factor rates, and daily or weekly remittances.

Reconcile loan balances to lender statements and maintain an accurate payoff schedule for every financing obligation.



AP, AR & Reporting



Manage accounts receivable, monitor due dates, and follow up on outstanding invoices.

Process accounts payable on time or ahead of schedule, and maintain an organized vendor and approval system.

Complete month-end close and deliver monthly financial statements (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow) with a written summary for the Owner.

Assist with budgeting and expense management.

Coordinate with our CPA for quarterly and annual filings.



Qualifications:



5+ years of experience in accounting or bookkeeping, including managing books independently.

Advanced proficiency in QuickBooks, including bank feeds, rules, classes, and reporting.

Proven working knowledge of US federal and state payroll tax calculation, filing, and deposits.

Experience tracking business loans and financing, with MCA and/or Stripe Capital experience strongly preferred.

Experience building cash flow forecasts and job-costing or profitability reports.

Ability to work independently, manage your own deadlines, and bring solutions rather than questions.

Strong Excel/Google Sheets skills.

High integrity with confidential financial information.

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field preferred.



Preferred Skills:



Experience in service-based businesses, especially cleaning, home services, or field service.

Multi-entity bookkeeping experience.

Familiarity with Profit First.

Experience working on an EOS team (Scorecards, Rocks).



Apply Directly via this link

title: AI animation artist
description:
Hiring: 2D Animation Artist / AI Animation Specialist for a 25-Minute Film



Project Type: Freelance, Fixed Price

Duration: Approximately 25 minutes

Deadline: Flexible

Budget: Open to competitive fixed-price proposals



Project Description



I am looking for a skilled and creative 2D animator or AI animation specialist to help me complete a 25-minute animated film based on my original screenplay.



The animation style is similar to Family Guy, with recurring characters, dialogue, facial expressions, and storytelling.



I have already created approximately 4 minutes of animation using an AI animation platform called Socool. I have the original project materials, the complete screenplay, and the voice recordings.



I am looking for someone who can take over the production, improve the existing scenes, and complete the remaining film while maintaining visual consistency.



Scope of Work



1. Review the existing 4 minutes of animation and available project files.

2. Extend several existing scenes to include additional dialogue from the screenplay.

3. Improve character movements, facial expressions, timing, and synchronization with dialogue.

4. Create approximately 21 additional minutes of animation.

5. Maintain consistent character appearances, backgrounds, and animation style throughout the film.

6. Edit and assemble the complete film, including the supplied voice recordings.

7. Deliver a polished final video, along with editable project files.



Ideal Candidate



I am looking for someone who:



* Has experience with 2D character animation and AI-assisted animation tools.

* Can work with existing characters and maintain visual consistency.

* Understands storytelling, dialogue timing, facial expressions, and lip synchronization.

* Can use AI tools efficiently to reduce production costs.

* Has experience producing longer animated videos, not just short AI clips.

* Communicates clearly in English and works independently.



You do not need to use Socool. I am open to other tools and production methods that can achieve comparable or better results at a reasonable cost.



How to Apply



Please include the following in your application:



1. Links to 2 or 3 examples of animated videos you have created, preferably featuring character dialogue.

2. A brief explanation of the software and AI tools you would use.

3. Your estimated total fixed price in USD to complete the 25-minute film, including revisions and any AI software or generation costs.

4. Your estimated production timeline.

5. Whether you can work with existing animation assets and extend previously created scenes.

6. The number of revisions included in your quote.



Paid Test Project



Before committing to the entire project, I would like to commission a short paid test.



The test will involve extending an existing scene by approximately 20 to 30 seconds, using my original characters and additional dialogue from the screenplay.



Please also indicate your price for this test.



I will share the existing animation and relevant project materials with shortlisted candidates.



I am looking for a reliable, cost-effective collaborator who can deliver consistent quality throughout the entire film.

ALVULT is an Australian brand developing aluminium sporting tubes and homeware containers. Our initial launch focuses on protective fishing rod tubes.

s and follow-up sequences.

 delivery.

s and follow-up timing.

title: Sales Representative

Job Description: Sales Representative / Account Executive

Company: Rice Labs (
)

About Rice Labs

Rice Labs is a premier custom apparel production and manufacturing partner for brands, businesses, organizations, creators, and events. We bridge the gap between creative concepts and retail-ready finished goods. Operating out of a comprehensive production infrastructure, we handle everything under one roof—including garment sourcing, automatic screen printing, flat/3D embroidery, DTF transfers, custom cut-and-sew manufacturing, relabeling, and retail-ready packaging. We aren't just order-takers or brokers; we are production partners focused on quality execution, hand-feel, fit, and reliable delivery.

Position Summary

Rice Labs is looking for a driven, results-oriented Sales Representative / Account Executive to help expand our client base across clothing brands, corporate uniform programs, event organizers, and independent creators.

The ideal candidate understands apparel blank qualities, decoration methods (screen printing, embroidery, DTF), and the lifecycle of custom manufacturing. You will act as the crucial front-line link between our clients and our production floor—qualifying incoming project requests, consulting on garment and print specs, writing accurate quotes, and cultivating long-term client relationships that turn one-off drops into recurring production programs.

Key Responsibilities

 * Client Acquisition & Pipeline Management: Identify, outreach, and close new business opportunities with emerging clothing lines, corporate clients, event producers, and high-volume creators.

 * Consultative Sales & Scoping: Review incoming project inquiries, guide clients through garment sourcing options (blanks, weight, fit, budget), and recommend optimal decoration methods (screen printing, embroidery, cut-and-sew, DTF).

 * Quote Generation & Pricing: Prepare detailed, transparent, and accurate line-item quotes in coordination with production capabilities, minimum order quantities (MOQs), and turnaround timelines.

 * Cross-Functional Coordination: Partner closely with our internal production, art, and fulfillment teams to ensure client mockups, technical specifications, and artwork specs transition seamlessly from concept to print floor.

 * Account Retention & Growth: Manage existing client accounts, scale repeat capsule drops and staff uniform restocks, and support multi-location or split-shipment execution.

 * Market Awareness: Stay updated on blank apparel trends, retail pricing models, decoration tech advancements, and industry standards to better advise clients.

Qualifications & Requirements

 * Experience: 2+ years of sales, account management, or business development experience—preferably within the custom apparel, screen printing, promotional products, or fashion/textile manufacturing industries.

 * Industry Knowledge: Solid working knowledge of apparel decoration techniques (Plastisol/water-based/discharge screen printing, 3D puff embroidery, DTF), fabric weights, fits, custom labeling, and retail finishing.

 * Communication Skills: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills; ability to explain technical production timelines and specifications clearly to clients ranging from indie creators to corporate procurement teams.

 * Organizational Mindset: High attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple fast-moving quotes, art approvals, and production pipelines simultaneously without letting details slip.

 * Tech-Savvy: Comfortable utilizing CRM software, quoting platforms, project management tools, and collaborative workspace apps.

What We Offer

 * Competitive base salary plus an attractive commission/bonus structure tied to sales volume.

 * Hands-on involvement in a growing production operation working directly with cutting-edge streetwear brands, creators, and businesses.

 * A collaborative work environment where your input directly influences production scaling and client success.

Rice Labs is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status.

ABOUT US



StayAscend engages this coordinator, for work across two small US businesses. TeamKekoa is Kekoa's real estate team: it helps buyers take homes from under contract, through escrow, to closed, and it runs the renovation that often follows. StayAscend is Jeremiah's short-term rental hosting company: it furnishes and sets up a finished home, launches it on Airbnb and Vrbo for its owner, and hosts every stay.



Part of your week is real estate transaction coordinator support for TeamKekoa, at Kekoa's direction: you work alongside TeamKekoa's transaction coordinator on files from under contract to closed and through renovation, with the deadline calendar, the title company, the lender, the inspections and the closing checklist, then the renovation paperwork. The rest of your week is StayAscend's launch work. For StayAscend you carry each home through the hosting agreement paperwork, the launch budget and the launch countdown, until it is live and handed to our operations team. Most days are a contract summary, a deadline calendar, a DocuSign status, a spreadsheet, a purchasing cart, a permit portal and a follow-up list. Put simply, it is contract to close and escrow coordination support, executive assistant work for two principals, and short-term rental and vacation rental launches, all on US hours.



Some homes have work in both, and where they do, one coordinator holds the whole story of the home. Kekoa usually has several homes under contract or in renovation at once. StayAscend has about nine homes launching this quarter and ten launch budgets open at the same time.



We automate what software can do. What software cannot do is notice that the lender and the title company wrote two different dates for the same closing, or that a budget line reads "sheet sets, all beds" and will never buy a single sheet. Noticing that, and saying so the same day, is this seat.



WHAT THIS ROLE REALLY IS



It is coordination with real deadlines and real money on both sides of a closing, for two principals, done by one person.



THE TRANSACTION HALF, AT KEKOA'S DIRECTION.



A home under contract carries a stack of dated obligations: an option period, a financing deadline, an appraisal, title work, a survey, inspections, lender conditions, a walkthrough and a closing. Each one has a date, a time and a time zone, and the contract itself says how its dates are counted.



- An option period that ends at 5:00 PM Central on a Thursday ends at 3:00 PM US Pacific, inside your window. The title company, the lender and the inspector each run their own calendar, so you ask each of them for status two days before, in writing, with that date and time in the message.

- Lender conditions come in rounds, and somebody has to carry each one from requested to cleared.

- When two sources disagree about a date or a figure, you do not pick the one you like. You find out which is right, from the document that governs it, and say so with the source attached.

- The most dangerous
 in a closing looks routine: new wire instructions, the day before closing, from a name you recognize.

- Renovation runs on paper: insurance certificates, signed agreements, lien releases, a change-order log and a draw log. A draw released before the paper is on file is a payment with nothing behind it.



THE LAUNCH HALF. Every case in this part is real. The amounts are changed. The shapes are not.



- A $16,742.19 furniture order was placed 14 days before the owner's money arrived. The rule since then: nothing is ordered until the owner's money has landed and the agreement is executed. You check both before a cart ever reaches Jeremiah.

- A home walked toward guest-ready with zero sheet sets on any bed. The plan's line for them read "sheet sets, all beds", one folded row, so no single set was ever bought, and the row still looked funded. Every line now gets split by size, with quantities counted from the house, before the first cart is built.

- $1,388.06 of tech for one home shipped to a different house and sat there for two weeks before anybody matched it to its plan. Deliveries are matched to the plan by packing slip, never by ship-to address.

- A hosting agreement was voided because the entity name the owner typed was not the entity on the deed. When you notice a mismatch like that, it goes to Jeremiah the same day. It never gets quietly corrected.

- An internet install takes 2 to 4 weeks, so the launch countdown starts with internet.

- A permit renewal was filed one day before expiry. The city's FAQ still described a 90-day grace period. The ordinance itself had deleted it. You read the source document, never the summary of it.



The honest description of this role: a deadline calendar and a budget record for every home in flight, kept true every day, plus a follow-up list that never gets as short as you want it to.



The person who is great at it reads the contract summary before anybody asks, counts the beds before building the cart, and sends the status request two days early instead of the afternoon of. They would rather write "I have not confirmed that yet, here is how I am confirming it" than a tidy guess.



This is not task-list work. The board, the deadline calendar and the countdown tell you what is next, because you keep them.



If this reads as a lot of chasing people who should have answered the first time, this is probably not your seat, and that is a fine answer. If it reads as a set of puzzles with dates on them, keep reading.



WHAT YOU WILL OWN



Seven stages, in the order a home moves through them. The first four are TeamKekoa's work, done at Kekoa's direction. The last three are StayAscend's work, done at Jeremiah's direction.



STAGE 1, THE PIPELINE. TEAMKEKOA ONLY. SUPPORTING KEKOA.



- Keep Kekoa's pipeline tracker current: every home his team is looking at, where it stands and what happens next.

- At Kekoa's direction, pull the facts into the workbook: listing details, comparable sales, the city's short-term rental ordinance, zoning, HOA documents and insurance quotes. For each source, write a short summary of what it says, with the link. Comparable sales are listed as found (address, date, price, link), never summarized into a value or a range.

- Not yours: every decision, every offer, every price and every opinion of value. Those are Kekoa's.



STAGE 2, UNDER CONTRACT. SUPPORTING TEAMKEKOA'S TRANSACTION COORDINATOR.



- Build the deadline calendar from the executed contract, using the dates and the counting rules that contract states. Anything unclear goes to Kekoa as a question, never into the calendar as your guess.

- Send reminders and document-status requests to the title company, the lender and the inspectors, in writing, ahead of each date.

- Schedule the inspections and the appraisal. Kekoa or the seller's side arranges entry for each, never you, and no lockbox or door code passes through you.

- Track every open lender condition from requested to cleared.

- Request short-term rental insurance quotes through the buyer's own insurance contact, and track the binder into the file before closing.

- Not yours: negotiation, any question about what the contract means, and any change of terms. Those go to Kekoa the same day, with the deadline. Buyers upload their financial documents straight to the lender's or the title company's secure portal. You never receive them.



STAGE 3, CLOSING. SUPPORTING TEAMKEKOA'S TRANSACTION COORDINATOR.



- Schedule the final walkthrough and the signing.

- Compare the closing disclosure figures against the checklist and flag every difference to Kekoa. You flag. You do not explain or resolve.

- Record that the buyer verified the wire instructions by phone, directly with the title company.

- Prepare the utilities transfer list, log the keys and remotes in the property record, and file every closing document in the property folder. Access codes live only in the access system, never in an
 or a chat.

- Not yours: wire instructions, ever. Any utility form that asks for a Social Security number, an EIN, a date of birth or a deposit is completed by the owner, Kekoa or Jeremiah.



STAGE 4, RENOVATION.



- Confirm each contractor's license, insurance certificate, signed agreement and lien release are on file before work starts or a payment is released.

- Keep the renovation schedule, the change-order log and the draw log.

- Draw requests: you log the amount, the date and whether the lien release is on file, never the bank or remittance details, which go straight to the principal who pays. A contractor who says their bank details changed is wall 2: you tell the principal by call or text the same day, and never reply to confirm anything.

- Prepare permit packets for the contractor or the owner to sign and submit, and schedule the inspections.

- Compile a weekly photo update from the on-site contractor.

- Not yours: running the work. The construction lead and Kekoa do that. Every draw is approved and released by a principal. W-9s go from the contractor straight to the bookkeeping route, and you never collect or store one.



STAGE 5, THE HOSTING AGREEMENT PAPERWORK. STAYASCEND.



- Jeremiah sets the terms and sends the hosting agreement. From then on you track its signature status on the board and prepare the onboarding checklist. You never open the envelope or the agreement.

- Once Jeremiah has marked it Completed on the board and sent his introduction
, you send the owner the welcome checklist on behalf of whoever holds the owner relationship (Jeremiah today, our operations lead once that seat is filled), and chase the items that carry no sensitive data: an insurance certificate that names the right insured, utilities in the owner's name, invitations to our software, and the house facts.

- Not yours: prospects, and every owner whose agreement is not yet Completed. Those are Jeremiah's, untouched. So are terms, fees, earnings and forecasts. Bank, tax and identity documents (the ACH form, a W-9, an ID) go through the secure route, never through your inbox.



STAGE 6, THE LAUNCH BUDGET RECORD.



The money record for every launch is yours, from the first line to the close-out. You never move the money.



- The tracker for every launch, current every working day.

- The item list split by size before the first cart: no folded rows, quantities counted from the house.

- Carts built and verified line by line, item code and quantity, for Jeremiah to place.

- Every order confirmation reconciled to the plan, to the cent, and every delivery matched by packing slip, never by ship-to address.

- The receiving calendar: a named receiver and a real date for every delivery, before anything ships.

- The close-out: the final reconciliation of plan, orders, charges and deliveries, ready for Jeremiah.

- Not yours: placing orders and moving money. Jeremiah approves and places every order and moves every dollar. Nothing is ordered before the owner's money has landed and the agreement is executed. The design belongs to the designer. Anything new an owner asks for after signing becomes a fixed-price proposal that Jeremiah sends.



STAGE 7, THE LAUNCH COUNTDOWN TO HANDOFF.



- Keep the countdown board from Completed to go-live, every date real and every gate current.

- Internet first, because the install takes 2 to 4 weeks. Then utilities, permit status (issued, not applied), tax-account status, the insurance certificate, photos, the listing staged in Hostaway, cleaner sourcing and vetting, and the guest-ready checklist.

- Hand the home to our operations team at go-live, with its file complete.

- Not yours: publishing a listing, engaging a cleaner or any vendor, and any conclusion about permits, tax or what is legal. Those are Jeremiah's, or our operations lead's once that seat is filled. The live home, with its guest messages, reviews, cleaning schedule, maintenance and owner reports, belongs to our guest and operations teams.



HELPING BUILD THE SYSTEM. You will improve both businesses' checklists out of your own work, writing down why each step exists so the next person does not learn it the hard way.



THE PRIORITY RULE, AND HOW THE WEEK RUNS



- First: a dated contract deadline. Option period, financing, appraisal, closing. It beats everything else in the seat.

- Second: a launch date with a guest already booked.

- Third: everything else, in board order.

- When two asks collide and the rule does not settle it, you say so in writing to both Kekoa and Jeremiah the same day, and you ask. You never silently pick one.

- When the work does not fit inside your window, you say that too. You flag it. You do not absorb it with unpaid hours.



How the week runs:



- One shared task board for both businesses. Every ask lives there, so neither principal has to wonder what you are doing for the other.

- One written weekly update to both of them, every Monday: what closed, what moved, what is at risk and what you need.

- Same-day written escalation for anything that cannot wait until Monday.

- No standing meetings. We work in writing by default.



WHAT YOU WILL NOT DO, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SECTION IN THIS POST



Six walls. All six are deliberate, all six are permanent, and none of them bends for a deadline, a friendly voice or an emergency.



Wall 1 is the law where our homes are, not our house style. So are parts of walls 4, 5 and 6, which touch privacy law, insurance rules and the rules on contacting owners and letting people into homes. The rest are our rules, and we hold them just as hard.



WALL 1. NOTHING THAT NEEDS A REAL ESTATE LICENSE: YOU SCHEDULE, TRACK AND FILE, YOU NEVER NEGOTIATE OR ADVISE.



You work at Kekoa's direction on everything in a transaction, and you never do the part of it that belongs to a license holder. Not once, not with a deadline an hour away.



- You never negotiate, on anything, with anyone. Not a repair, not a credit, not a date.

- You never answer a question about what a contract means, or about whether to use a right in it. Not for the buyer, not for the seller's side, not for the title company.

- You never give an opinion of value or of price, even a casual one. You never solicit a buyer, a seller or an owner. You never let anyone into a property.

- What you do instead: you schedule, track, remind, file and prepare, at Kekoa's direction. Any question about terms goes to Kekoa the same day, in writing, with the deadline stated in his time zone and in yours.

- The reason: in Texas and in other states, that work belongs to a license holder, and the rule reaches both the assistant who does it and the person who directs them.



WALL 2. PAYMENT INSTRUCTIONS AND BANK DETAILS: YOU RECORD THAT THE BUYER CHECKED, YOU NEVER TOUCH THE INSTRUCTIONS.



Wire instructions, payment instructions and bank details never pass through your hands, in any form, for any reason, however urgent the message sounds.



- You never send, forward, type, verify or change wire instructions, payment instructions or anyone's bank details. Not for anyone, and not to anyone, a principal included. Bank or remittance details on a contractor's draw invoice go from the contractor straight to the principal who pays, never through you.

- Any change in payment instructions is treated as fraud, including a contractor who says their bank details changed. For a buyer's closing funds, only the buyer confirms, by calling the title company on the number in its opening package or on its website. For anything either business pays, a principal confirms by phone on a number already on file. A new
 from a familiar name is not a confirmation. Neither is a reply to that
.

- You never call a phone number that came in the suspicious message. That number belongs to whoever sent it. You tell the principal by call or text and say where the message sits.

- The reason: wire fraud at closing is the single most expensive
 crime in real estate, and the losses are rarely recovered.



WALL 3. MONEY: YOU BUILD AND VERIFY, YOU NEVER MOVE A DOLLAR.



Nothing you do places an order, charges a card, releases a draw or reaches a bank. Not in an emergency, not to catch a sale.



- You never place an order. You build the cart, verify it and hand it to Jeremiah, who approves and places it.

- You never make a charge, a payout, a draw, a deposit or a refund. You have no access to banking or accounting, on purpose. If you ever find that you can somehow reach one, you do not act. You report it.

- You never mark a cart ready to place before the owner's money has landed. You check that first, every time.

- The reason: the person who records money is never the person who moves it. That is what makes your record worth trusting, and when money goes somewhere it should not have, it cannot have been you.



WALL 4. BANK, TAX AND IDENTITY DATA: YOU POINT TO THE SECURE ROUTE, YOU NEVER OPEN THE FILE.



Sensitive personal data does not live in this seat: not in any inbox, folder, chat or spreadsheet you touch.



- You never ask for, open, forward, type or store a Social Security number, an EIN, a W-9, a date of birth, an ID, bank or card numbers, or a buyer's financial documents.

- When one arrives anyway, you do not open it or forward it to anyone, a principal included. You point the sender, warmly, to the secure route, and you tell the principal the same day where the message sits, so it can be removed.

- The reason: it protects owners' and buyers' identities, and it keeps you out of the blast radius if a file ever leaks.



WALL 5. TERMS, NUMBERS AND CONCLUSIONS: YOU GATHER THE SOURCES, YOU NEVER DRAW THE CONCLUSION.



Anything with a number or a conclusion in it comes from a principal, never from you.



- You never quote or explain a fee, a term, an expected earning or a forecast. Not a range, not "around", not confirming a number somebody said first.

- You never contact a prospective owner, or any owner whose hosting agreement does not yet show Completed on the board. Until it does, even after Jeremiah has sent it, every conversation with that owner is his.

- You never sign an agreement or press send on one, for either business.

- You never draw a legal, permit, zoning, tax or insurance conclusion. Whether a home may host guests is never yours to answer. You gather the sources and summarize what each one says, and the decision belongs to a principal, or to counsel.

- The reason: anything with a number or a conclusion in it is a promise the business has to keep, so the person who makes it has to be the person who can keep it.



WALL 6. ENGAGING AND PUBLISHING: YOU PREPARE EVERYTHING, YOU NEVER COMMIT EITHER BUSINESS.



Nothing you do commits either business or gives anyone a way in. Not for a contractor who is ready to start, not for a vendor already at the door.



- You never engage, hire or sign anything for either business: not a contractor, a cleaner or a vendor.

- You never publish or change a live listing. You stage it completely and hand it over.

- You never give an access code to anyone except, after closing, through the access system to a dispatched vendor or a guest of record. Before closing, Kekoa or the seller's side arranges every entry.

- The reason: commitments and access are principal decisions, and neither business can take back a code given to the wrong person.



Read all six walls as protection, not as distrust. They protect you, the owners, the buyers and both businesses, and they are what let two businesses open their files to one person. We will not ask you to bend them, and if anybody else ever does, the right answer is a warm no and a message to us the same day. We think they are one of the best parts of this seat.



A WORD ABOUT CONFIDENTIALITY



You will see a lot: purchase prices, closing figures, buyers' names, what owners are spending on their launches, what we pay vendors. None of it leaves either business, for any reason. That includes an owner who asks what another owner paid, a contractor who asks what the last bid was, and anybody being very friendly about it. If that is not a line you can hold comfortably, please do not apply.



The other direction matters just as much. No side deals with a vendor, a contractor, a title company or anyone else. Nothing that benefits you or anyone connected to you. No splitting a purchase so it sits under a limit. And you never create a mail forwarding rule or a filter on any account you use for this work, because a hidden forwarding rule is exactly how criminals read, and quietly redirect, closing
s. If you find one you did not create, you report it the same day. Any of these is immediate cause, even when the purchase or the rule turns out to have been harmless.



WHO THIS IS NOT FOR



- Not a guest messaging or customer support seat. That team already exists.

- Not the transaction coordinator on a file. TeamKekoa has one; you support that work.

- Not the owner's ongoing contact after go-live. Our operations team is.

- Not a negotiator, a closer or a salesperson.

- Not on site. Anything physical goes to a local contractor or contact, and you coordinate it.

- Not a bookkeeper. You never touch the books or the bank.



MUST-HAVES



We will not ask you to describe yourself with adjectives. These are the things that predict the work.



- 2+ years coordinating US real estate transactions from contract to close. Files you personally carried, not files you helped somebody else carry. The form asks how many you carried in the last 12 months.

- You have built a deadline calendar from an executed contract and kept it true while the dates moved: option period, financing, appraisal, title, closing.

- Hands-on DocuSign, plus at least one of Dotloop, SkySlope or a similar transaction platform.

- You chase people who do not report to you and have no reason to answer: title officers, lenders, inspectors, contractors, delivery companies. We will ask how many times you followed up on a real one and what you changed each time.

- When two sources disagree, you find out which is right from the document that governs it, and you say how you know.

- Real spreadsheet skill, not "proficient in Excel" on a resume. Lookups, SUMIFS, filters, spotting a typed number where a formula should be, and a total exact to the cent.

- You can tell somebody senior that a date will not hold or a number is wrong. Early, in writing, with the evidence attached.

- You can work for two people at once without making either of them chase you.

- You hold a line when holding it is awkward. The seller's side will ask you something friendly that you are not allowed to answer. So will an owner. Declining warmly and routing it fast is the skill.

- HONEST, AND THIS IS THE HARD GATE. If you have not confirmed something, you say so. You never report a status you did not verify, and you never invent a date, a figure, a confirmation or which home a delivery belongs to. "I do not know yet, here is how I am finding out" is always the right answer. This is the most important item on this list, and we test it at every stage.

- Written English that a US title officer, lender and homeowner read as clear and professional. Most of this seat is writing.

- Stable power and internet, with a real backup you can describe.

- The ability to work the fixed graveyard window in the hours section below, in both seasons, indefinitely. Please read that section before you apply.



NICE-TO-HAVES



- Texas transactions. Kekoa's team will show you how its contracts set their dates, so this is a plus and never a requirement.

- Airbnb, Vrbo, Hostaway or PriceLabs, as a host, a co-host or an assistant to one.

- Renovation paperwork: insurance certificates, lien releases, change orders, draw logs, permit packets.

- Furnishing purchasing: building carts, reconciling order confirmations, tracking deliveries to a vacant house.

- A city permit portal or a short-term rental registration you saw through to issued.

- A checklist or tracker you built that somebody else then ran without you in the room. Not required. Rewarded.



TOOLS YOU WILL USE



- Google Workspace: Sheets for the trackers and launch budgets, each business's own Drive for its own property folders, Gmail and Calendar.

- DocuSign, and the transaction platform Kekoa's team uses for the contract-to-close files.

- One shared task board for both businesses (StayAscend uses 
 today; the shared tool is not yet chosen), and Slack. Transaction cards carry no buyer names, prices or figures, which stay in TeamKekoa's own folders.

- Hostaway, our hosting software, where listings are staged, feeding Airbnb, Vrbo and 
.

- Amazon Business, Wayfair, Walmart and Home Depot, where you build carts that Jeremiah places.

- Matterport scans, and city permit and tax portals, which differ by city.

- The access system, where door codes live. Nowhere else.

- No access, on purpose: the accounting system, the banks, the payment processors, the Airbnb, Vrbo and 
 host accounts, and checkout or any saved card on a store account.



HOURS AND TIMEZONE



This is a fixed availability window on US Pacific time. Please read the conversion carefully, because the Manila hours change twice a year.



- The window is 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM US Pacific, Monday to Friday. Eight hours a day, forty hours a week.

- In Manila that is 11:00 PM to 7:00 AM while US daylight time is on (the second Sunday of March to the first Sunday of November), and 12:00 midnight to 8:00 AM the rest of the year.

- The arithmetic. While US daylight time is on, Manila is 15 hours ahead of US Pacific: 8:00 AM plus 15 hours is 11:00 PM, and 4:00 PM plus 15 hours is 7:00 AM the next morning. The rest of the year, Manila is 16 hours ahead: 8:00 AM plus 16 hours is 12:00 midnight, and 4:00 PM plus 16 hours is 8:00 AM.

- The US changes its clocks and the Philippines does not, so US Pacific is the fixed one, and every deadline we send you is written in US Pacific.

- In Manila your working week starts Monday at 11:00 PM while US daylight time is on, and at 12:00 midnight as Monday turns into Tuesday the rest of the year. It ends on Saturday morning: 7:00 AM while US daylight time is on, 8:00 AM the rest of the year.

- It is a graveyard shift. You sleep during the day, every working day.

- Why this window: it is 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM in Texas (US Central), so you overlap most of a Texas title company's and lender's working day, and 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM on the US East Coast, so East Coast vendors are reachable until they close.

- The window is fixed, and it does not quietly grow. No weekends and no on-call. If a contract date falls on a weekend, the work is to have it handled inside the window before it, and to make sure Kekoa knows.



If 11:00 PM to 7:00 AM Manila while US daylight time is on, and 12:00 midnight to 8:00 AM Manila the rest of the year, does not fit your life, please do not apply. That is a reasonable answer, and we would rather hear it now than in week three.



COMPENSATION



- $1,000 per month, flat. That is the monthly service fee for the work in this post and the availability window above.

- About $5.77 an hour: 40 hours a week times 4.33 weeks is 173.2 hours a month, and $1,000 divided by 173.2 is $5.77.

- One short independent contractor agreement, with StayAscend, which pays the whole fee. One board, one weekly written update.

- Paid on the 1st and the 15th of each month, in US dollars, through Wise, to an independent contractor based in the Philippines.

- The first 4 weeks are an Initial Evaluation Term, paid as a weekly engagement fee of $185 per week (4 times $185 is $740). After that the monthly service fee starts, with the first period prorated.

- Access builds up over those 4 weeks: you shadow in week 1, work supervised with a daily review in week 2, and work in full with a daily review in weeks 3 and 4.

- A merit review 90 days after you move onto the monthly service fee, then once a year.

- No bonus is promised, and nothing is ever paid per closing or per sale. That is deliberate, and it follows from wall 1.

- You supply your own computer, internet, backup power and workspace. We supply the business accounts the work runs in: the mailboxes, the board, the trackers and the logins.

- We treat our people well, and the good ones grow with us.



HOW WE HIRE



Five stages, then a paid trial. Every stage is done on your own time, and no call is scheduled until you have already shown us how you work.



1. The application form. About a dozen questions, 30 to 40 minutes.

2. A 2-minute unscripted video and two voice recordings of about 60 seconds each, within 48 hours. The request is
ed to you automatically when your form arrives, so check your spam folder. Send links that open for anyone with the link: YouTube set to unlisted, or Google Drive set to "anyone with the link". A late reply, a link we cannot open, or a reply without the video in it ends the application.

3. A written scenario exercise, within 72 hours of the invitation. Six situations drawn from this seat, answered in writing, in your own words. This is the stage that d
 the seat. We score every exercise within a week of receiving it.

4. A short, free work-style questionnaire. You
 us a screenshot of the result. It is a tiebreaker and a guide for the interview, and nobody is cut on it.

5. An interview of about 45 to 60 minutes, scheduled around your window. Then two reference checks. Each reference has to confirm the dates and the scope of your work, and one who cannot is a fail, so line them up now.



Then, for the final two or three, a paid trial: $75, about 2 to 3 hours, on invented files, never on real owners or buyers. We need a W-8BEN form on file before we can pay it.



There is no application window and no waiting for a batch. Each stage opens when you finish the one before it, and every clock is measured from the
 that reaches you, which states your own exact deadline. We do not grant extensions, because in this seat the deadline is the job. We also answer you at every stage, including when the answer is no.



Please do not use AI to write any of your answers. This process asks about files you carried, people you chased and deadlines you saved or missed. A model has to invent those, and it invents the same ones for everybody. Grammar mistakes cost you nothing here. An answer with no real file behind it costs you everything.



HOW TO APPLY



Fill out the form linked at the very bottom of this post.



Applications sent any other way will not be reviewed. Please do not message us on this platform, do not
 us, and do not send a resume in a reply. Only form submissions are looked at.



The last question on the form checks that you read this post. It is not a code word and there is nothing to look up. You just have to read it carefully.



Mahalo,

The StayAscend Team
